log: DNA ROTATION AND WHERE THE ENERGY GOES
Displacement is one projection of the response and it hides two things. TWIST is a degree of
freedom translation does not capture, and it travels along a rod rather than through space --
the mechanism of supercoiling -- so it may carry a mark much further than the ~15 A
displacement reach measured earlier. ENERGY says what is STRAINED rather than what moved, and
strain at the DNA-histone interface is mechanical coupling to how tightly the DNA is held,
which is the closest thing to accessibility this line has produced.
1KX5 no waters: 13625 atoms, 263765 springs | 84 base pairs resolved by C1'-C1'
baseline twist: 45.92 deg/step (sd 29.96) over 83 steps
= 7.8 bp per turn, against ~10.5 for ideal B-DNA.
Reported as the control it is: change is measured against THIS helix, not against the ideal.
TWIST CHANGE by SEQUENCE separation from the mark (degrees, RMS over steps in each bin).
Separation is in BASE PAIRS, not Angstroms, because torsion travels along the helix.
WHERE THE STRAIN IS STORED. `share` is the compartment's fraction of the springs -- only
the RATIO is evidence, since a channel holding 20% of the energy while being 20% of the
network has done nothing selective.

TWIST DOES NOT BEAT THE SHUFFLED CONTROL AT RANGE: whatever rotation appears far
from the mark is what the rod does for any force, not something the mark carries.
INTERFACE LOADING IS 0.01x ITS SHARE -- strain distributes with the network's
own connectivity rather than concentrating on the grip, so the accessibility bridge
is NOT supported by this evidence and should not be assumed downstream.
